payload.because: The home is ALREADY in the truth log — session_started names it uniquely — so an index file would be duplicated state that can desync, needs pruning (99 sessions and counting), and forces a SPEC Record-layout change plus a gitignore decision (routing is a local runtime fact, but .sofar/ is committed wholesale). Deriving costs one file read on the common path (branch is correct → hit on the first log checked) and only pays the sibling scan in exactly the case where a misroute would otherwise have happened; total log volume is ~350KB. It is also self-healing: sessions registered before this fix get pinned correctly with no migration. Same philosophy as reading git state rather than logging it — a fact with an authoritative home is read, never copied.
payload.chose: Derive a session's home initiative from the event logs themselves — scan for the session's earliest session_started, checking the branch-bound initiative first and only falling through to siblings on a miss
payload.over: A new .sofar/sessions.json index mapping session_id to slug, written at registration and read by hooks

payload.because: The defect was not repetition, it was the window: checking only s.ended >= me.started bounds below and not above, so an ENDED session kept reporting siblings that wrapped after it closed, forever, on every prompt. An ended session is not working and has no window for anything to have wrapped inside — one guard removes the whole class. Keeping it stateless preserves the design property that made the line cheap. Budget order is the same kind of fix: the summary is the least actionable field and was rendering first, so it clipped away the next action; reserving the tail costs nothing and cannot regress.
payload.chose: Bound the parallel-wrap window by this session's own liveness (skip entirely when me.ended is set), and compose next_action + push state before the summary so the summary absorbs the leftover budget
payload.over: Adding a "already told you" marker to suppress repeats, or widening the 420-char budget
